goal: the game content of the rulebooks that the completeness check found missing (Р-242)
extra:
## This work (Р-242, Р-230, Р-51)

The completeness check (`checks/20261114-completeness/`, files `verify-rules.md`, `verify-malleus.md`, `verify-scenarios.md`) found game content of these books that the base does not hold. Your unit takes exactly the items of its `target`; read the matching rows of those verify files first — they say what is covered (do not duplicate) and what is missing or partly there.

Rules of rule and table records (as in the Keeper Rulebook work, Р-175, Р-171):
- One `rule` record per section of the book: a heading of a section inside the chapter («Боевой раунд», «Броня», «Фаза развития сыщиков»); its small subsections go inside the same record (`text`, `steps`, `tables`, `examples`). A section that is only a lead-in of one line joins the next section.
- `id` — `coc:rule:<slug>`, slug from the English name of the section in Keeper Rulebook (`keeper-rulebook-en`), lower case with hyphens; file `kb/rules/<slug>.json`. Before creating a file, check that `kb/rules/<slug>.json` does not exist; if another unit could own the same subject, prefer the more specific slug (`chase-movement`, not `movement`).
- `category` — one of the schema's; `optional: true` only where the book says «необязательное правило».
- A table with a die roll (1d10, 1d20, 1d100…) is a `table` record (`kb/tables/<slug>.json`, Р-171) referenced from the rule's `refs`; a table without a roll stays in the rule's `tables`.
- `refs` — existing records only (skills `coc:skill:*`, characteristics `coc:characteristic:*`, tables, other rules, spells, tomes); check every id exists in `kb/`. Links to rules that other units are writing now: use the slug you expect only if you are sure of it, otherwise leave it out and list it in the report.
- Text and every number from the page image of the Russian Keeper Rulebook (`python pipeline/source/pages.py image keeper-rulebook-ru <printed page>`); the text layer is noisy. Printed page = «с. N» of pages.py, physical = «физ. M»; check that the number on the page image is N.
- `name.en` and a second source from `keeper-rulebook-en` (printed page = physical − 1; pages.py does it).
- Examples of play in the book — `examples`, in full. Keeper advice without mechanics belongs in records of the chapter «Ход игры» only; elsewhere keep it inside the rule's `text`.
- The owner's Foundry journals `checks/20261107-foundry/journals/*.md` are hints only: never take their additions that are not in the book.
- Records already done and yours to keep consistent with: `kb/rules/poisons.json`, `kb/rules/suffocation-and-drowning.json`, `kb/rules/other-forms-of-damage.json` (combat unit owns them and may improve them), `kb/tables/*.json` (bouts of madness, phobias, manias, hit locations) — do not duplicate them.
- Coverage: in `checks/20261114-completeness-fix/<your unit name>.md` list every section heading of your pages → the record that holds it (or «не взято» with the reason).

For the English books (Malleus Monstrorum, Grand Grimoire, Pulp Cthulhu): numbers and facts from the English page (`python -B pipeline/source/pages.py show <book_id> <page>`, check numbers on `pages.py image`); the Russian text is our translation (flag `translated`); official Russian forms of names — glossary `python -B tools/terms.py <word>` and existing records (Р-184). `id` slugs — from the English heading; look at a few existing records citing the book for `axes`.

Shared records (kb/creatures, kb/spells, kb/weapons, kb/rules…) that already exist: your unit may edit only the files listed in its `owns`; for any other existing record write a proposal (`pipeline/integrate/README.md`). Adding lore to an existing creature: put the article's narrative (history, theories, other names, cult) into the record's description/legend fields as the schema allows, add the Malleus page to `sources`, keep everything already there.

New spells (`kb/spells/<slug>.json`, `coc:spell:<slug>`): model `kb/spells` records that cite grand-grimoire-en; cost and casting time as printed; check first that the spell is not there under another name (Grep by the English name in `name.en` and `aliases`, and by the Russian name).

Weapons with 1930s prices (Pulp): `cost` has the key `1930s` (Р-242). A weapon that exists (from the Keeper Rulebook) gets the 1930s price and a Pulp source; a model that does not exist (Beretta 1938A, Lewis Mk VI…) is a new `coc:weapon:*` record; a price list without dice is a `table` or rule `tables` as the rules above say.

Coverage: in `checks/20261114-completeness-fix/<your unit name>.md` list every item of your target → the record that holds it (or «не взято» with the reason).
